Title: Historia Ecclesiae Malabaricae cum Diamperitana Synodo apud Indos Nestorianos, S. Thomae Christianos nuncupatos, coacta ab Alexio de Menezes Augustinensi an. Dni MDXCIX, nunc primum e Lusitano in Latinum versa; cui accedunt cum Liturgia Malabarica tum Dissertationes variae, omnia perpetuis animadversionibus illustrata
Creator: Johannes Facundus Raulin, O.S.A. (Jo. Facundus Raulin Caesaraugustanus, Ordinis Eremitarum S. Augustini), author of the Historia Synodi Diamperitanae, the notes and the Dissertationes, and translator of the Synod's acts into Latin; by his own preface the acts are rendered from the Portuguese archetype printed at Coimbra in 1606 in Antonio de Gouvea's account of Menezes's journey. The acts themselves are the work of the Synod of Diamper (1599) under Aleixo de Menezes, Archbishop of Goa
Publisher: Romae: Ex typographia Hieronymi Mainardi, superiorum facultate
Publication Date: 1745 (title page 'ROMAE, MDCCXLV'; approbation dated Rome, 27 April 1745)
Rights: Public Domain (published 1745, more than 95 years before 2026; public domain by date)
Language: lat
Source: Internet Archive item bub_gb_GwYeoa5XibsC, file bub_gb_GwYeoa5XibsC_djvu.txt (Google scan of the National Central Library of Rome copy), fetched directly by the library/source-research thread (Era VII session), 2026-10-16; host rights statement: licenseurl http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark 1.0); no possible-copyright-status field.
Provenance note: Header prepended; the OCR text follows unchanged apart from this header (no long-s characters present; the OCR renders the eighteenth-century long s as 'f' throughout and that pattern is left as found; nothing retyped, dropped or corrected; Google page markers left in place). Rights basis restated in one checkable sentence: the title page inside this file reads 'ROMAE, MDCCXLV', so the work is public domain by date.
Content note: Latin throughout. Printed order: dedication, preface (Praefatio, where Raulin states his sources and his translation method), 'Elogia et testimonia' on Menezes and the Synod, index of contents; 'Historia Synodi Diamperitanae' in four chapters (Raulin's own history, drawn mainly from Gouvea: Malabar affairs sacred and profane, events before the Synod, the Synod's course, events after it); 'Synodus Diamperitana', Actio I-IX, the acts and decrees in Raulin's Latin, with his running notes; the letter of Andreas, Bishop of Cochin, to the Synod and the Synod's reply; 'Liturgia Malabarica Menesiana', the Mass of the Malabar church as revised at Diamper ('Sacrum Beatorum Apostolorum'), with Raulin's Admonitio and notes that profess to mark the Synod's alterations; Dissertationes I-V on the apostolate, martyrdom and relics of St. Thomas and on the Malabar church. The Synod's text is primary evidence in its Latin rendering; Raulin's history, notes and dissertations are eighteenth-century Roman scholarship. OCR sampled at 10/30/50/70/90 percent and found readable but rough (share of word-like tokens 0.77, many broken words, marginal notes interleaved); a second scan of the same edition (1745_Historia_Ecclesiae_Malabarica_Cum_Diamper, kerala-archives) sampled worse. Second witness for exact wording until a passage is checked against the page images. No public-domain English translation of Raulin exists; the acts are in English in Geddes 1694 and Hough 1839 (both vendored), and the Malabar liturgy in Neale's English (liturgies-eastern_mark-james-clement-chrysostom-basil-malabar_neale-1870s.txt).
